author: Ryan Blessing Sun staff writer
title: Westerly to apply for up to $625K in Community Development Block Grant funds | Daily-news-alerts | thewesterlysun.com
text:
WESTERLY — The town is preparing an application for as much as $625,000 in funds from the Community Development Block Grant program for four different initiatives and programs.
The largest, $375,000, would go toward a Park Avenue infrastructure project. A new water main, sidewalks, drainage structures and roadway would be installed between Newton Avenue and Spruce Street.
It's the one town project in the application package, which also typically includes yearly requests from the WARM Center, Westerly Education Center and the Jonnycake Center, Town Manager Shawn Lacey said.
"The drainage there goes back well over 100 years, so I'm told," Lacey said of the Park Avenue work, which is concentrated on lower Park Avenue.
This year, WARM is requesting $70,000 to help support the overhead costs for the center's housing stabilization services. The Jonnycake Center application is for $50,000 for staff costs associated with the center's Community Resource Office.
The Community College of Rhode Island's Westerly Education Center is applying for $130,000 to help fund medical assistance training at the Westerly location.
Part of the CDBG application process involves sending the requests to a local public hearing. That is scheduled for 6 p.m. Nov. 2 at Westerly Town Hall, in the council chambers. The town is the applicant for all the CDBG requests, Lacey said.
"The town has to be the applicant," for the Education Center, WARM and Jonnycake requests, Lacey said. "But these are their asks and we partner with them on the application."
The Community Development Block Grant program was established in 1974 and operates under the requirement that all grant-funded activities meet one of three national objectives: Benefiting low- and moderate-income persons, preventing or eliminating slums or blight, or meeting other community development needs having a particular urgency because existing conditions pose a serious and immediate threat to the health or welfare of the community and other financial resources are not available to meet such needs.
Federal funds are allocated yearly to the state, which awards eligible activities within the categories of public facilities/improvements and public services, including job training, through a competitive application process.
